page.layout: One page of text: verse poem at top in italic, a signature line "IO. IACOMOTVS BARRENSIS.", then a rule, then a heading "EPIGRAMMA GEORGII Buchanani iam olim ad Th. Bezam scriptum." followed by a verse poem in italic with an initial P. Single column; no margin notes.

p.i:
Quòd tendat arces, quaque decent pias
Mystas, & Virgentis senectæ
Damna leuant miseranda, Christum
Spirare toto pectore gestiat:)
Parêre iussis talibus haud licet,
Nec luce fas vnquam labores
Perpetua violare dignos.

Qua scripta quondam iusserat ignibus
Sanis aduri grandiloquus Maro,
Seruauit Augustus, vetusta
Fata Getans iterare Troiæ.

main_text.head: EPIGRAMMA GEORGII Buchanani iam olim ad Th. Bezam scriptum.

p.i:
PRasul optime, sacra Christiana
Qui caste colis & facis canisque,
Ad te carmina mitto, nec Latino,
Nec Graio satis tincta, sed Britannis
Nata in montibus, horrida sub arcto,
Nec cælo neque seculo erudito.
Quasi iudicio tuo probentur,
Ut classis modo in vltima referri
Possint centurias, nihil timebo
Censuram inuidia, nihil morabor
Senatus critici seueritatem,
Nihil grammaticas tribus: mihi Vnus
ia est curia, ce nfor, & Quirites.

page.notes: Doubtful readings in the verse: "Quòd"/"Qua" initial letters; "Virgentis" and "Getans" uncertain; "ia est curia, ce nfor" is a damaged line, partly illegible; the first line of the second poem's stanza "PRasul" has an enlarged initial P. Printed letters with long s rendered as s. Italic type throughout the verse.
